Can you tell me more about the incident?
Axle counters are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. They count train wheels as they enter and leave a section of track, allowing the signalling system to confirm when that section is clear.
If an axle counter fails, the signalling system may show that a train is still in the area even when the section of track is clear. This means the signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and get permission from the signaller before passing the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely if they see anything ahead of them. This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.

Thameslink between Cambridge and Brighton
nrIncident.message:
There is a fault with the signalling system in the Meldreth area. This means that trains will run at a reduced speed on some lines.
As a result, trains running between Cambridge and Hitchin may be cancelled, delayed by up to 20 minutes or revised.
This is expected until 10:00.
Customer advice:
Due to a fault with the signalling system in the Meldreth area, your journey may be subject to delays or alterations due to services through the area running at reduced speeds.
How the service is affected:
Some services that normally run between Kings Lynn and London Kings Cross and will now run a shuttle service between Kings Lynn and Cambridge. Please allow up to 30 minutes additional time to complete your journey.
Services that normally run between Cambridge and Brighton have been suspended.
Services that normally run between Cambridge and London Kings Cross will continue to run and make additional stops at Ashwell & Morden where possible.
If you are travelling between Cambridge and London, it may be faster to take a Greater Anglia service to London Liverpool Street. You can then connect to London St Pancras International using London Underground services at no extra cost.
Please allow up to 30 minutes additional time to complete your journey.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• Greater Anglia services between Ely and London Liverpool Street
• Alternative Great Northern and Thameslink services between Kings Lynn, Cambridge and London
• London Underground services between London terminals
For the latest information, check station screens and use our online journey planners.
Planning your journey:
You can see live maps of the network here:
• Great Northern live map
• Thameslink live map
These maps will now show where your journey is likely to be delayed.
You can also use the Thameslink or Great Northern apps to get more information about your journey.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
Axle counters are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. They count train wheels as they enter and leave a section of track, allowing the signalling system to confirm when that section is clear.
If an axle counter fails, the signalling system may show that a train is still in the area even when the section of track is clear. This means the signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and get permission from the signaller before passing the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely if they see anything ahead of them. This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Axle counters are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. They count train wheels as they enter and leave a section of track, allowing the signalling system to confirm when that section is clear.
If an axle counter fails, the signalling system may show that a train is still in the area even when the section of track is clear. This means the signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and get permission from the signaller before passing the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely if they see anything ahead of them. This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.

nrIncident.message:
On Friday 23 October, a freight train partially derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking. Some lines remain closed as significant damage has been caused to the railway infrastructure.
As a result, some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised. Where trains do run there may be delays of up to 10 minutes.
• London Overground are running a reduced service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham and no trains will run between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside.
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex), and Purfleet
Disruption is expected until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 10 November.
A visual disruption map video is available.
c2c customer advice:
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet.
Trains which normally call at Stratford (London) and London Liverpool Street will divert, and call at West Ham and London Fenchurch Street instead. These trains typically operate after 20:30 each evening, and at weekends.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• Elizabeth line services between London Liverpool Street and Romford
• First Essex buses between Grays and Stanford-le-Hope
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London), and Liberty line services between Upminster and Romford
Replacement buses are running from 05:00 between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham, Purfleet and Grays.
Replacement buses are running from 05:25 between Grays and Upminster, calling at Purfleet, Rainham and Upminster.
Passengers for Dagenham Dock can travel on the EL2 bus service at no extra cost.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside.
A reduced service will run between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham as follows:
• Services will depart Gospel Oak at xx:09 and xx:39
• Services will depart South Tottenham at xx:13 and xx:43
Your ticket can be used at no extra cost on:
• London Buses via any reasonable route
• London Underground via any reasonable route
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey for today using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner. For journeys from Friday 6 November please check back later.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Lines reopened: disruption between Cambridge and Hitchin expected until 16:00
nrIncident.routes:
Great Northern between Kings Lynn / Ely / Cambridge / Royston and London Kings Cross
Thameslink between Cambridge and Brighton
nrIncident.message:
Following a fault with the signalling system in the Meldreth area all lines between Cambridge and Hitchin have now reopened. As service recovers, trains may be cancelled, delayed by up to 15 minutes or revised.
This is expected until 16:00.
A visual disruption map video is available.
Customer advice:
Services may continue to be altered, cancelled or delayed by up to 15 minutes.
Services between Ely and Kings Lynn are still disrupted and you will need to allow an additional 60 minutes to complete your journey on this route.
How the service is affected:
Some services that normally run between Kings Lynn and London Kings Cross will run between Kings Lynn and Cambridge only.
Some services that normally run between Cambridge and Brighton have been cancelled.
Services that normally run between Cambridge and London Kings Cross will continue to run and make additional stops at Ashwell & Morden where possible.
Please talk to station staff, look at information boards or check your journey planner for the latest information.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• Greater Anglia services between Ely and London Liverpool Street
• Alternative Great Northern and Thameslink services between Kings Lynn, Cambridge and London
• Southern services between London and Brighton
• Gatwick Express services between London and Brighton
• London Underground services between London terminals
For the latest information, check station screens and use the online journey planners.
Planning your journey:
You can see live maps of the network here:
• Great Northern live map
• Thameslink live map
These maps will now show where your journey is likely to be delayed.
You can also use the Thameslink or Great Northern apps to get more information about your journey.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
Axle counters are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. They count train wheels as they enter and leave a section of track, allowing the signalling system to confirm when that section is clear.
If an axle counter fails, the signalling system may show that a train is still in the area even when the section of track is clear. This means the signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
The fault has been fixed and services and recovery of the scheduled timetable is in progress, however, due to drivers and trains having been displaced, some trains may still be cancelled or altered.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
